older.text: If I ask you to check something later, can you keep track of it?
older.reply:
Yes, in two ways:

1. If you give me a specific day/time ("check X tomorrow at 9am"), that's handled as a reminder — I'll come back and answer it at that time on my own, no need for you to message me again.

2. If it's more of a standing instruction or an open task without a fixed time ("keep an eye on X" or "let me know when Y happens"), I hold it as an open commitment and act on it across future messages rather than forgetting it when this conversation moves on.

The honest limit: I don't have a background process that proactively polls the outside world on its own — "checking" something only works if it's checkable with the tools I have here (files, shell commands, reading the public web) or at the moment a scheduled reminder fires. If what you want checked requires a logged-in account (email, a dashboard, etc.), I don't have access to that without it being connected first.

If you've got something specific in mind, tell me what it is and when/how often, and I'll set it up now rather than in the abstract.
